subject: This week in rentals — rates eased, 3 deals worth a second look
preheader: 30Y settled at 6.84% · 3 deal-spotter notes from PHL, IND, MEM · New: house hacking math

marketSnapshot.headline: Rates eased on softer jobs print, summer rents firming
marketSnapshot.body: The 30-year fixed dropped 12bp this week after a softer-than-expected May jobs print. Asking rents in our top-10 covered markets ticked up 0.4% MoM — small move, but it's the third consecutive month of positive rent reads, which we haven't seen since late 2024. Watching whether June numbers confirm a real summer firming or just a seasonal blip.

dealSpotter.body: $420k ask, two units both already rented at $1,950 each. Taxes are reasonable for Philly (~$5.8k), no HOA, recent roof. Pencils at 8.2% cap and $1,650/mo net cash flow with 25% down. Watch the 1925 build year — budget $4-5k year-one capex even at the discount.

$185k 3/1.5 ranch, rents at $1,475 per the local manager. Working class neighborhood, school rating C+. Numbers are clean but the area's appreciation tailwind has slowed since 2023. Better as a yield play than an appreciation bet.

Listing screams cash-flow gold ($1,300 + $1,150 + $1,150 / $245k) but the DSCR drops to 1.04 at current investor-loan rates with realistic vacancy + capex assumptions. If you can land it 8-10% under ask AND verify all three tenants are paying, this becomes a Decent. As-is, walk.

blogFeature.title: House hacking explained: how to (almost) live for free in a 2-4 unit
blogFeature.excerpt: The full math behind FHA 3.5% down vs conventional 5%, the year-2 transition where break-even flips to real cash flow, and what to look for in a property that pencils as both a primary residence and an eventual pure rental.

qa.question: Should I refi out of my 7.5% rate now if rates drop to 6.5%?
qa.answer: Run break-even on closing costs ÷ monthly savings. On a $300k loan, a 100bp drop saves ~$200/mo at typical 30Y terms; closing costs of $5-7k means break-even in 25-35 months. If you plan to hold past break-even, refi. If you're selling in 18 months, don't. The other variable: do you have other debt that's higher? If credit card balance is sitting at 22% APR, the refi might unlock a cash-out that saves you more than the rate drop alone.
